overview.heading: How the Book Cover Maker works
paragraphs: Enter the title, an optional subtitle or series line, and the author name. Choose a genre and, if you have one, describe the cover image you imagine. PiCraft designs a front cover that follows the visual conventions of that genre, with the title large enough to read as a thumbnail in search results.

Genre matters because readers recognize a book's category in a fraction of a second. A thriller in pastel watercolor, or a romance in dark metallic type, sends the wrong signal and can lose the readers it was written for.
You download a 1600×2560 px eBook cover that matches Kindle's ideal size, and a 6.125×9.25 inch front cover at 300 DPI that includes bleed for a 6×9 inch paperback.

whatYouGet.title: 1600×2560 px eBook cover
whatYouGet.description: A JPG at the ideal Kindle cover size and the 1:1.6 ratio, in RGB.

whatYouGet.title: 6×9 inch front cover with bleed
whatYouGet.description: A 6.125×9.25 inch image at 300 DPI, with bleed on the outer, top and bottom edges, for use as the front panel of a paperback cover.

whatYouGet.title: Genre-appropriate design
whatYouGet.description: Ten genres, from fantasy and thriller to memoir and children's books, each with its own look.

whatYouGet.title: Title, subtitle and author
whatYouGet.description: Type is set large and legible, with the title dominant and the author name clear.

whatYouGet.title: Your cover idea
whatYouGet.description: Describe a scene or symbol and the cover is built around it.

useCases.title: Self-published Kindle books
useCases.description: Get a first professional-looking cover for a novel, a short story collection or a nonfiction title.

useCases.title: Series branding
useCases.description: Use the same genre and similar wording on each book so a series looks related.

useCases.title: Lead magnets and short reads
useCases.description: Make an eBook cover for a free guide, a workbook or a newsletter bonus.

useCases.title: Concept testing
useCases.description: Compare a few cover directions before you commission a designer or order a final print.

useCases.title: Draft covers for paperbacks
useCases.description: Produce the front panel for a designer or a printer template, and add the back cover and spine afterwards.

tips.title: Choose the genre honestly
tips.description: Readers browse by genre. Pick the one your book fits, not the one that sounds most impressive.

tips.title: Use a short title
tips.description: Short titles can be set larger. If your title is long, put the extra words in the subtitle.

tips.title: Describe one strong image
tips.description: "A lighthouse on a cliff at night, a girl with a lantern at its base" gives a clear central picture. Lists of many objects make covers busy.

tips.title: Test it at thumbnail size
tips.description: Shrink the image to about 160 px tall. The title should still read, and the image should still be recognizable.

tips.title: Keep the series line short
tips.description: A subtitle such as "Book One of the Tidewater Saga" works because it is brief.

tips.title: Look at covers in your category
tips.description: Search your genre on Amazon and compare. Your cover should feel at home on that page while still standing out.

tips.title: Generate more than once
tips.description: Each generation is a different design. Try a few and choose the one that is both beautiful and clear.

styleGuide.heading: Choosing a genre
styleGuide.intro: Each genre follows the cues readers expect, such as the colors, the type style and the kind of image.

items.title: Fantasy
items.description: Rich illustrated scenes, dramatic skies and ornate lettering. See the [fantasy book cover maker](/create/book-cover-maker/fantasy).

items.title: Thriller / crime
items.description: Dark tones, strong contrast and bold sans-serif or condensed type. See the [thriller book cover maker](/create/book-cover-maker/thriller).

items.title: Romance
items.description: Warm, bright covers with an emotional focus and flowing or script type. See the [romance cover maker](/create/book-cover-maker/romance).

items.title: Science fiction
items.description: Space, technology and cool colors with sleek or futuristic type.

items.title: Nonfiction / business
items.description: Clean layouts, clear titles and simple graphic images.

items.title: Literary fiction
items.description: Restrained, artistic covers with a single strong image.

items.title: Horror / dark
items.description: Shadows, unsettling imagery and a limited palette.

items.title: Memoir
items.description: Personal, atmospheric images with a quiet, readable title.

items.title: Children's book
items.description: Colorful illustration, rounded shapes and friendly type.

items.title: Historical fiction
items.description: Period-appropriate scenes, muted colors and classic type.

checklist.heading: Before you publish the cover
items: Check the spelling of the title, subtitle and author name against your book details.
Shrink the cover to thumbnail size and confirm the title is readable.
For a light or white cover, add a thin grey border so it does not disappear on Amazon's white page.
Make sure you have the right to publish the imagery commercially.
Confirm you disclose AI-generated content if the store you publish on asks for it.

For paperbacks, build the full wrap with your printer's template and place the front file as the front panel. The [KDP paperback cover size](/sizes/kdp-paperback-cover-size) guide shows where the fold lines fall.
Keep text at least 0.125 inch inside the trim line of a paperback, as KDP recommends.

limits: The maker produces a front cover only. It does not create the spine, back cover or barcode.

A printed paperback needs a full wrap sized to your page count and paper. Use the printer's template for that, and see the [KDP paperback cover size guide](/sizes/kdp-paperback-cover-size) for the formula and spine widths, or the [book cover size guide](/sizes/book-cover-size) for the eBook specs.
KDP requires paperback covers as a single PDF with back, spine and front, so the front file needs to be placed in a template.
The text is part of the image. To change a word, generate again.
AI-generated images may not qualify for copyright protection in some countries.
